newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixs barely changed, market pauses.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixs barely changed, market pauses.

text.p: The precious metal markets held their steady tone on Friday but a reaction to the surge higher earlier this week was not ruled out, dealers said.
"Where we finish tonight will probably dictate the tone for next week," one dealer said.
The markets were also conscious of an early finish on New York's Comex tonight ahead of a U.S. holiday on Monday and the expiry of March gold and silver options after close of business.

Gold was fixed at $342.40 per ounce just 10 cents down from the morning setting in a market which had locked into a narrow range all day. At the fixing Comex April was showing a rise of $1.60 at $344.60.

There was no obvious reaction to the fresh items of news which came into the market earlier including a statement by the Belgium National Bank governor that Belgium would not sell any more gold from its reserves.

The dollar held above 1.68 marks but was near intraday lows by 1515 GMT and taking some of the heat off gold. The January producer price index was a surprise 0.3 percent down while industrial output was unchanged.
A dealer described losses in platinum and palladium as "normal profit taking" after a statement from Moscow that Russia and Japan could begin talks on 1997 platinum and palladium supply details.
A resumption of shipments could start in April with the possibility of larger shipments initially to make up for first quarter losses, dealers said.
"I can't believe there is not going to be a (price) correction," one analyst said.
Platinum was indicated at $364.80/$365.80 down $1.70 and palladium was $3.50 lower at $133.50/$134.50 having fixed at its highest level in 11 months on Thursday at $141.25.
Silver held on to an overnight gain of two cents at $5.15/$5.17 with dealers keeping an eye on movements on Comex ahead of the March option expiry after close of business.
They said open interest was heavy on the $5.00 puts and even heavier on $5.25 calls.
"A close near $5.20 would be very interesting. They could go for the calls which has happened before ahead of a U.S. holiday," one dealer said.
All the Comex markets are closing early tonight. Palladium and copper close at 1800 GMT, silver at 1805 GMT and platinum and gold at 1810 GMT.
